title: StegVerse Foundations
summary: A guided tutorial series for understanding the purpose, principles, mechanics, authority boundaries, evidence model, and practical operation of the StegVerse ecosystem.

modules.title: What Is StegVerse?
modules.objective: Explain the ecosystem purpose and distinguish governance infrastructure from an intelligence provider.

modules.title: Your StegVerse Identity
modules.objective: Understand StegID, identity continuity, devices, and receipts.

modules.title: Your Knowledge Vault
modules.objective: Understand KV custody, references, privacy, and recovery boundaries.

modules.title: Devices and Nodes
modules.objective: Understand device registration, node establishment, continuity, and node state.

modules.title: What Happens When You Press Submit?
modules.objective: Trace a candidate action across Interlock/InTr without conflating submission, admission, execution, or evidence.

modules.title: Understanding Authority
modules.objective: Distinguish capability, authority, observation, admission, execution, and evidence.

modules.title: How StegCore Governs a Transition
modules.objective: Understand represented constraints, candidate transitions, governance decisions, and evidence.

modules.title: Reading a Receipt
modules.objective: Understand provenance, correlation, reconstruction, and what a receipt can and cannot prove.

modules.title: Heartbeat and Runtime
modules.objective: Understand HB/oscillator observability and why liveness signals do not grant authority.

modules.title: AI Inside StegVerse
modules.objective: Understand AI participation, human involvement, and governance separation.

modules.title: SKAP and Capabilities
modules.objective: Understand capability custody and why possession, reference, admission, and authority are distinct.

modules.title: Crossing the Ecosystem Boundary
modules.objective: Understand governed interaction with external systems and reciprocal interoperability.

non_capture_note: Completing this path demonstrates exposure to ecosystem concepts; it does not establish permanent competence, identity, authority, or permission.
